page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is an Intel-based x86_64 compute instance equipped with 2 vCPUs across 1 physical CPU core using hyperthreading. It features dedicated CPU allocation and 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The processor includes 260 MB of L3 cache along with support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX tile and int8 extensions, and hardware-accelerated cryptography primitives. The instance includes no attached local storage, no dedicated GPU accelerators, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluation indicates moderate single-core processing capabilities, reflected by average scores in Geekbench single-core tests (1836.0) and single-threaded compression workloads. However, overall multi-core throughput is limited due to the 2-vCPU hardware footprint, resulting in lower scores on multi-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench software compilation tasks. Memory performance shows restricted bandwidth on large blocks (17.81 GB/sec uncached read) and a lower PassMark memory score, highlighting cache dependence for intensive data operations.

From a resource allocation standpoint, the server offers dedicated compute execution without memory overhead, presenting a lean profile for tasks requiring consistent single-threaded execution rather than high concurrency or large memory buffers. Its lack of included local SSD storage requires network-attached persistent disks for stateful applications. Suitable workload fits include lightweight microservices, basic web serving, utility scripts, background task processing, and small-scale development or testing environments where memory demand remains low.
